articles.title: 'The Mosquito Bowl' Producer Alex Gayner Thought He'd Solved Every Problem a Set Could Throw at Him. Then Came a Runaway Parrot.
articles.summary: Ten seconds of footage ended up being the most nerve-wracking part of the shoot for the movie veteran who has been on sets since the '90s.
articles.content:
Filmmakers often thrive on controlled chaos. Alex Gayner has spent his career orchestrating that madness.

Long before producing The Mosquito Bowl for Peter Berg , Gayner cut his teeth doing odd jobs on '90s direct-to-video actioners — the kind of movies you'd stumble across on a pay-cable channel at 1 AM during a bout of insomnia. Then, a second AD was let go before lunch, and Gayner found himself promoted on the spot. It was an unlikely break that set the course for the rest of his career.

He gradually climbed the ranks to first assistant director, eventually trading B-movies for some of the biggest studio productions around, including Guillermo del Toro’s Pacific Rim and Gareth Edwards’ Godzilla . He also developed a reputation as a closer, overseeing reshoots for Suicide Squad (2016), Birds of Prey , Zero Dark Thirty and Mulan , among others. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV 'Beef' Creator Lee Sung Jin Launches Production Company, Plans Ali Wong Limited Series Movies Ray Nicholson Levels Up With 'The Mosquito Bowl': "I'm Always Battling for Legitimacy"

Another turning point arrived in the late 2010s, when the native New Yorker decided to pivot to producing. If the first AD is the on-set quarterback who executes plays on the field, then Gayner wanted to become a full-time offensive coordinator, the person drawing up the plays and mapping out the production behind the scenes.

He credits Nicolas Winding Refn with giving him his big break as a producer on the 2019 limited series Too Old to Die Young , an opportunity that paved the way for him to produce the first season of Beef and win an Emmy for his work. (Gayner and Refn are now assembling the latter’s long-gestating Maniac Cop movie, which recently received approval for a California tax credit.)

After wrapping Beef , Netflix pointed Gayner toward Berg’s 19th-century Western limited series American Primeval . But first, the two had to bridge the gap between the producer Berg expected and the one Gayner turned out to be. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“When I met Pete, I don't think he really knew what kind of producer I was,” Gayner tells The Hollywood Reporter . “Naturally, he didn't know if I was going to come in to watch the money or try to make the show on soundstages. We had to figure each other out.”

To keep the football metaphors going, Berg likes to run his sets with a no-huddle offense, frequently calling audibles along the way. He might improvise dialogue, change camera positions or throw out the playbook altogether. Most of all, he has a strict devotion to immersive, practical filmmaking. Fortunately, Gayner has been adapting on the fly ever since that lunchtime promotion more than 30 years ago. He also shares Berg’s preference for capturing as much as possible in camera.

Thus, they quickly got on the same page for American Primeval , setting the stage for two features, The Mosquito Bowl and the highly anticipated Call of Duty video game adaptation.

“That [adherence to practical] really solidified our relationship as filmmaking partners. He knew I wasn't afraid to go back to the old-school way of how we learned to do things,” Gayner says. “It’s a little uncomfortable to get that realism and that immersive, visceral experience on film, but it’s worth pushing the envelope.”

The Mosquito Bowl , based on a novel by Berg’s cousin Buzz Bissinger, chronicles four real-life college football players who enlisted in the U.S. Marine Corps during World War II and played in a fabled 1944 football game known as the Mosquito Bowl alongside 60 other former collegiate players turned soldiers. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Berg and Gayner threw Nicholas Galitzine, Bill Skarsgård, Ray Nicholson and Tom Francis into football crash courses with help from San Francisco 49ers All-Pro running back Christian McCaffrey, the New York Giants and two of the industry’s best on-set football coordinators. Then they dropped the actors into the ocean and jungle of Queensland, Australia, doubling for Japan, while surrounding them with tanks, explosions, flamethrowers and blank gunfire.

Berg wanted to honor one specific character detail that belonged to Nicholson's Tony Butkovich, the former Purdue University fullback who was drafted in the first round by the Cleveland Rams. Bissinger wrote about how Butkovich sent photos home of himself with a parrot on his shoulder, so Gayner received the unenviable task of finding what would become the one-and-only available parrot on the island continent. The bird was still young, and its wings had to be clipped to prevent catastrophe during filming.

After months of planning and training, cameras finally rolled on Nicholson and the supposedly grounded parrot. Within seconds, the parrot flew off into the 100-foot-tall trees. Its four wranglers panicked, as did the rest of the stunned cast and crew. Gayner, meanwhile, tried to counter Berg’s fatalism with optimism.

“Pete looked at me and said, ‘I know exactly what’s going to happen. The headline of every entertainment paper in L.A. is going to be, “Peter Berg Kills Parrot During Filming of The Mosquito Bowl .”’ And I said, ‘No, Pete, we’re going to find the parrot.’” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Hours later, they managed to retrieve the parrot from a tree and tie a string to its leg as an added precaution until they got the necessary shots. The ordeal amounted to roughly ten seconds of footage in the final cut, but it’s a stark reminder of how much labor goes into even the briefest moments in a film.

“We can control actors, special effects and stunts. But when the only parrot in Australia that’s available for our movie flies away, you're stuck,” Gayner says. “We didn't want to use a CG parrot. We'd made that commitment.”

Below, in a conversation with THR , Gayner elaborates on training two British actors and a Swedish actor to play a sport they’d never played before, let alone understood.

Your filmography is overwhelming. You’ve seen some things, haven’t you?

( Laughs .) I’ve seen a few things, yeah. I've been around the block. I've gone from tiny little things to big giant things — and everything in between.

I can only imagine the war stories you must have, especially as first assistant director. That’s widely considered the most stressful job on set. First ADs are often regarded as the quarterback to the director's head coach. Did you have any kind of support group with your fellow first ADs?

Not really, because first ADs never work with other first ADs. You can talk to each other, share experiences and discuss your approaches to working with directors, but you never really get to spend time with them, especially on a movie set, unless there's a first and second unit. Everybody has such different styles. But it is a stressful job. It's a heavy-lifting job. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I started making films in Hollywood when I was 20 years old, and I worked for a very low-budget film company that made straight-to-video action movies. They filmed one movie every three weeks. So we would do 18-day shoots — three consecutive six-day weeks — with the exact same crew. We'd wrap a movie on a Friday, and then we'd start a new movie on a Monday. You'd get the script midway through one movie, and everybody would just roll onto the next film. I did that for three years, and I made 30 films in three years.

I did everything from driving the grip truck to learning how to load film, because we were still shooting film at the time, to being a boom person and working with the grips and the electric. So it really was my film school, and it taught me so much about what everybody does on a film set. Then I just happened to fall into the AD department because a second AD got let go. At lunch, they were like, "Alright, you're now the second 2nd." And I was like, "Okay, I'll figure out how to do that." Eventually, that happened with the [first] AD.

Why do you think these assistant director roles fit you so well?

I have a knack for communicating with all the departments and rallying everybody to have a common vision. And as I started to become a first AD on smaller movies before eventually doing some second-unit action sequences and working my way up to the bigger studio films, I made it less stressful for myself. I really understood what everybody was up against and what everybody was doing. I didn't want to live under that constant pressure of only being focused on, How are we going to make our day? How are we going to get the schedule done? We have to just keep going. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

That is part of the job, but really, I'm a filmmaker. I want to participate creatively in supporting the story and the characters. And as a first AD, if you can figure out how to do your job and motivate the crew — while working in a respectful environment with a couple hundred people, keeping them on the same page and being a good creative partner to the director, the producer and the studio — it takes a lot of the pressure off. You're not being this machine butting up against an artist trying to birth something that's in their brain.

So, as a first AD, I was always a creative first, and I figured out how to translate that into the schedule, the days, the shot lists and the time that the DP had to light. Integrating myself as a creative partner to everybody made it less stressful and more enjoyable.

Another pattern in your work is that you tend to assistant-direct a lot of additional photography. Examples include: Suicide Squad, Birds of Prey, Zero Dark Thirty, Mulan and Total Recall. That’s a fraught period of time since the production is spending the last of its money, and there’s a lot riding on the additions and/or revisions. Was there a reason why your number kept getting called for reshoots? Are you the Winston Wolf of reshoots?

( Laughs .) I don't really know the answer. Part of it was schedule and circumstance. Another part of it was word of mouth. I really took pride in what I did as a first AD, and I'm a very even, mild-mannered first AD. There are some who are not. Everybody has their own style, but I always was very balanced and very calm in the pocket, so to speak, to go back to your quarterback reference. So I think that reputation just got around town. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid6' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Also, if a director’s usual first AD wasn't available for reshoots, I tended to be on the short list to be called. It was very flattering. It was a really great way to build relationships with other directors without having to commit a year or two to the overall process, and it expanded my résumé quite a bit.

You’d produced here and there prior to 2023, but did your Emmy for producing Beef season one lead you to produce full-time? It looks like you stopped assistant-directing that same year.

I’d been going back and forth before producing Beef . The last movie I AD’d was Spiderhead with Joe Kosinski during COVID. It was a very hard transition. I'd worked so long to be successful as an AD, and then I looked in the mirror and went, "Alright, I'm going to stop doing this and make the transition to producer." With a family and a mortgage, it was a big commitment to step into a new role, essentially starting at the bottom. But I knew that it was the natural next step, something I had to do and really wanted to do. The project that got me really confident as a producer was a limited series called Too Old to Die Young that Nicolas Winding Refn directed.

Big fan. Every time I see Nell Tiger Free, I remind her how haunting her beach scene with Miles Teller is.

I absolutely remember that day. We went up to the [Mugu] rock at the end of Malibu, right on the turn there. It was a wild show, and I loved making it. Nick originally called me to AD the series, and I turned him down because I was really committed to producing. But he kept calling me and calling me. And I said, "Nick, look, I really appreciate it, but I have to stick to this. I have to make this transition. This is what I'm going to do." In 2017, limited series really weren't that big a thing yet, and Amazon, under Roy Price, was also still finding its legs. This was long before Jen Salke came in. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid7' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Then Nick said, "I'll tell you what, I'm going to direct this entire series by myself, which I've never done before. If you AD the first episode of the show for me, I'd love for you to produce the series. Once you get me on my feet, then you can produce the rest of the episodes. I just need you to prep for me and help me with casting and finding locations."

So we figured out what would work for him and what would work for me, and we made a deal. I AD'd the first three weeks or so, and then I stepped off the set. Other ADs then came in, and I produced the rest of the show. Nick wrote the series with Ed Brubaker, and besides directing all the episodes, he was editing every night. So he was at it seven days a week, 20 hours a day.

It was a fantastic experience and one of the most creative things I've ever been a part of. It was such a specific vision that he had. We shot most of it in L.A. over a hundred days. It was a very small-budget show, and we stretched every dollar. That was really the beginning of producing for me.

Do you think Maniac Cop is ever going to happen?

I’m as sure as I can be. It just qualified for the California Tax Credit. It got approved. He's making it as a film instead of a series. We tried to make it as a series for HBO. We were very close to making it, but once COVID hit, it was just impossible to make that kind of show at the time.

You wrapped Beef season one in 2022. In 2023, you EP’d American Primeval for Pete Berg. Did you hit it off to such a degree that he wanted you to be his boots-on-the-ground producer and UPM for The Mosquito Bowl ? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid8' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

American Primeval was a very complicated show to make out in the elements for a hundred-plus days. I was asked to come in as a non-writing EP. Pete and I had never worked together. I'd never even met him. I had previously worked with the other executive producer, Eric Newman, and I had a longstanding relationship with a lot of people at Netflix.

When I met Pete, I don't think he really knew what kind of producer I was. He's worked with a lot of the same people over the years, and he has this very raw, immersive, visceral vision of whatever he's making. So, naturally, he didn't know if I was going to come in to watch the money or try to make the show on soundstages. We had to figure each other out.

But as soon as we hit the ground in New Mexico, he learned that I have the same desire to make films and television as practically as he does. There are definitely benefits to going on stage and shooting blue screen for certain pieces, but for a huge sequence at the end that takes place on top of a snowy mountain, there was talk of going to a quarry-type setting and making fake snow in a very controlled environment. As soon as I started talking creatively with Pete about it, I knew there was no way this was going to work for what he was trying to do visually and what Mark L. Smith wrote.

My first reaction and suggestion to that proposed plan was, "I don't want to do that. I want to gather a lean crew with as little gear as possible, and climb up a mountain in the real snow. We can build a shack and do it for real, while having access and keeping everybody as safe and comfortable as humanly possible." To fabricate all that in the New Mexico summer and then add visual effects, it would've felt too different. Paper snow doesn't react to horses the same way as real snow, and that went for every element of that sequence. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid9' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

So that [adherence to practical filmmaking] really solidified our relationship as filmmaking partners. He knew I wasn't afraid to go back to the old-school way of how we learned to do things. It’s a little uncomfortable to get that realism and that immersive, visceral experience on film, but it’s worth pushing the envelope.

Pete is known for having a very vocal, energetic and off-the-cuff directing style. He’ll throw out alternate dialogue mid-take without cutting. How did you adapt your own process to his “no-huddle” manner of shooting a movie?

I didn't have to adapt that much. Working with Pete as a producer, it’s like creating an action-packed play. He's very improvisational. If something comes to mind on set, he goes for it. Being a First AD for so many different kinds of directors, as well as shooting additional photography, really served me as a producer. I learned how to step into a preexisting structure, whether for a couple of scenes or a whole sequence, and adapt to a crew that's already been through battle together. As a producer, I try to be as responsible for the active environment I'm creating as I am for the story.

Pete especially likes a 360-degree environment, and that's how I approach every project. There’s no cheating. You can’t go out to a location with all your trucks lined up behind you and say, "Okay, you can only look west." That 360 approach really slimmed everything down, allowing us to be nimble and giving Pete the freedom to say, "Okay, I want to turn around and look the opposite way.” It helped us discover some magic on American Primeval and The Mosquito Bowl . Organic pieces of the puzzle fell into place. The actors appreciated it, too. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid10' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Mosquito Bowl has numerous war and football sequences, which must have been a logistical nightmare. You weren’t the First AD on this set, but that experience must have served you well.

100 percent. Every challenging project I've produced has been made better by my experience and the tools I gained as a First AD. The Mosquito Bowl wasn't a logistical nightmare, but it was very challenging logistically. There were so many challenges to figure out on a daily basis that I had to use every tool in my toolbox.

When Pete started writing and talking about The Mosquito Bowl while we were shooting American Primeval , we agreed that if we were going to make a war movie, we had to do something different. So many amazing World War II films have already been made. We had to take responsibility for trying to capture even 0.1 percent of what these soldiers went through emotionally. Obviously, we would never compare what we do as filmmakers to what any soldier experienced in war, but we had to deliver something immersive, violent and shocking for the audience while remaining true to what really happened.

That meant putting the actors in the ocean instead of in a water tank or a pool and using real explosions and blank gunfire instead of visual effects. We had to find running tanks and develop hundred-foot flamethrowers. As a producer, I was never going to let “it’s impossible” come out of my mouth. There was always going to be a way to make it as real as possible, and that became our mission statement from the beginning. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid11' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

With every person we interviewed and every department we approached about joining The Mosquito Bowl , we said, "This is how we want to do it. We want to make this as real as possible. Can you do this? Are you up for it? And what are your ideas to help us get there?"

Did San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey consult you guys as far as how to train the actors to look like capable football players in just four weeks?

He absolutely did. Christian McCaffrey helped us build the foundation for the actors to become football players. Pete, who's friendly with Christian, gave him a call once we had Nicholas Galatzine, Bill Skarsgård, Tom Francis and Ray Nicholson on board. Christian is a beast. He’s one of the most amazing football players there is, and he’s such a gracious guy. He does so much work with veterans, and he’s involved with a nonprofit, so he was immediately willing to donate his time. He was even coming back from an injury at the time, but two days after Pete called him, he was on the field in Westlake with Ray, running plays, teaching him moves and consulting as a running back. Additionally, we sent Tom Francis to the New York Giants because he was doing Sunset Boulevard on Broadway, so he got to train with them.

We had two Brits, a Swede and one American, and with Ray being the American, he was the only one who had ever really played football. He played high school football and knew a lot about the game, but Nick, Tom and Bill didn't know much about it. So they worked tirelessly with our football coordinators, Mike Fisher and Don Powers, who have worked on a lot of football movies. They came down to Australia and ran a four-week camp with the actors, bringing in a ton of Aussie rules football and rugby players, as well as a few college football players from the States to fill in at quarterback. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid12' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

For all the football and battle sequences, ten seconds of a parrot interacting with Ray’s character was the task that put you through your paces the most?

( Laughs .) That put Pete through his paces more than anything else on the movie. I don't know about myself. Every single day, my brain was working at a hundred miles an hour trying to solve problems. Birds and animals in Australia are different from those in other parts of the world. You have some of the deadliest snakes and spiders, as well as bull sharks. Everywhere you go, you have to be aware of nature's pitfalls. So finding movie animals there was difficult, and Australia doesn't have every breed you might find in North America or elsewhere.

Ray’s character, Tony Butkovich, really had a parrot as a pet during World War II. That was based on real information. But finding a movie-trained parrot that looked the way we wanted was nearly impossible. We worked with animal wranglers who eventually found one, but it was very young. They had to train it so we could feed it.

They also clipped its swings so it wouldn’t fly away. We had to shoot the scene within a specific window before the parrot got old enough to learn how to fly. So we were up against the deadline of the parrot instinctively knowing how to fly. We also shot the whole movie in continuity, so our first AD, Andrew Ward, had to figure out how to fit the scene into that window. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid13' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

There had been months of logistical planning and training, and Ray had to understand what he could and couldn't do with it. Eventually, the day came when we had to work with the parrot. We were in the jungle, surrounded by smoke. Everyone was carrying guns and wearing all this gear, but everything had to be silent and still.

Gosh, all this for ten seconds of footage.

Yeah, when Ray sat down to do the scene, the set had to be cleared. Pete couldn't call action, and nobody could say a word. The animal wranglers put the parrot down next to Ray and made hand signals for the cameras to start rolling. Ray started feeding the parrot, and within two seconds, it flew off into the jungle. ( Laughs .) The parrot that wasn't supposed to be able to fly with its clipped wings disappeared up into the trees.

The animal wranglers freaked out, and we all had to stop and look up. We were looking for a tiny parrot in the Australian jungle, surrounded by hundred-foot trees and dense foliage. The animal wranglers then crawled through the jungle, making parrot noises and trying to call it back.

Pete looked at me and said, "I know exactly what's going to happen. The headline of every entertainment paper in L.A is going to be, ‘Peter Berg Kills Parrot During Filming of The Mosquito Bowl .’” And I said, "No, Pete, we're going to find the parrot." So the search went on for hours, and the animal wranglers stacked ladders and held pool cues with baskets on the ends. Eventually, the parrot came back and we got the shots, but it was one of the most stressful ordeals. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid14' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

We can control actors, special effects and stunts. We can have that kind of input. But when the only parrot in Australia that’s available for our movie flies away, you're stuck. We didn't want to use a CG parrot. We'd made that commitment.

You just proved why I’m endlessly fascinated by behind-the-scenes stories. Of all the projects you’ve been a part of, which one deserves the I Play Rocky treatment?

It’s between American Primeval and Too Old to Die Young , but it’s hard to pick one or the other because they're very different.

American Primeval was logistically the hardest project I've ever produced and made. We did it for real in the New Mexico desert through winter, spring, summer and fall, with no cover sets and no place to go, with horses and 1800s footwear and clothing, a writers' strike and a SAG strike. Taylor Kitsch, our lead actor, even broke his foot, and Betty Gilpin, our lead actress, got pregnant during the strikes before having to come back to finish the show. We went from shooting in one winter season with the heaviest snow in New Mexico to finishing the show the next winter season, and it was New Mexico’s warmest winter with no snow.

Too Old to Die Young was the most eccentric creative experience I’ve ever produced. Nick shot 10-minute-long takes where the camera didn’t move. We drove around Hollywood at three in the morning with John Hawkes and Miles Teller. They drove a police car by themselves up the 405 while I was in the backseat with a camera in my hand. A CHP officer followed us and allowed us to do that night after night. articles.title: James Gunn Should Return to Marvel to Wrap Up One Beloved MCU Character’s Story
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel When James Gunn entered the MCU with Guardians of the Galaxy, he was still relatively new to directing feature films, despite many years as a successful screenwriter. After all, he had directed only two movies at the time: 2006’s body horror thriller Slither and the 2010 superhero dark comedy Super. Neither targeted the same audience […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google When James Gunn entered the MCU with Guardians of the Galaxy , he was still relatively new to directing feature films, despite many years as a successful screenwriter. After all, he had directed only two movies at the time: 2006’s body horror thriller Slither and the 2010 superhero dark comedy Super . Neither targeted the same audience as the Disney-owned Marvel Studios, but the company took a chance on Gunn, trusting his artistic vision to turn the Guardians of the Galaxy from a relatively obscure comic book title to one of the MCU's marquee franchises. And it worked better than anyone could have imagined.

Over the course of the next decade, the Guardians of the Galaxy — the core line-up consists of Star-Lord, Gamora, Drax, Rocket, and Groot —would appear in two sequels to their own film, two Avengers movies, the fourth Thor film, an animated series, and a Disney+ holiday special. Gunn had turned the team into a pop cultural phenomenon, showing up everywhere from video games to theme park rides. Although Gunn’s history with Disney hasn’t always been the warmest in the business, now feels like the right time for Gunn to make a triumphant return to the MCU, if only to give fans one specific project they’ve been waiting for.

Fans often debate whether Gunn’s Guardians of the Galaxy trilogy is the best in the MCU. But one clear thing is that fans haven’t seen the last of the team, at least not all of them. Some of the series’ actors — such as Dave Bautista and Zoe Saldaña — have made it clear that they have moved on from Marvel. Other stars, such as Karen Gillan , still seem open to reprising their roles whenever Marvel Studios comes calling. But only one character was promised to make an appearance following Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 . As the film tells viewers, “The Legendary Star-Lord Will Return.” But when and where? Here's

Chris Pratt — who, of course, has played Peter Quill aka Star-Lord throughout the MCU — last appeared in the final post-credits scene of Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 . Having returned to Earth and reunited with his grandfather, Quill is seen enjoying a bowl of cereal with his grandpa. The moment carries a real “what now?” vibe, implying that perhaps Quill might struggle to adjust to a normal life on Earth after his intergalactic adventures. And while Pratt has reassured fans he will return at some point, Marvel has offered no indication of when or even where Star-Lord might reappear next. For all we know, Pratt could make a surprise appearance in Avengers: Doomsday or Avengers: Secret Wars .

Given how Star-Lord played a fairly instrumental role in the past two Avengers films, it’s likely he’ll be among those joining the fight against Doctor Doom. But even if he does appear in an ensemble film, that doesn’t mean it’s the end of Star-Lord’s time in the MCU. There’s a real opportunity for Marvel to delve deeper into the character than ever before in a Star-Lord spinoff film . Now that he’s returned to his home planet and reconnected with his humanity, what does Quill do after having left the Guardians? Will he make a solo run for it as a hero or link up with another team? If the MCU wants to answer those questions, it knows exactly who to turn to. And as it turns out, he will probably be available sooner rather than later.

In 2018, Gunn was unceremoniously fired from Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 , and even though he ultimately returned to complete his trilogy (as well as the aforementioned 2022 holiday special), Gunn soon left Marvel to accept a role as co-chairman and co-CEO of DC Studios. With his imminent departure from DC , it’s very possible Gunn could return to at least round out Star-Lord’s arc with a solo adventure. After so many years in the MCU, Pratt definitely has the fanbase to carry his own film. And like Black Widow , perhaps The Legendary Star-Lord will just happen later than expected. If it does, we’re certainly hoping Gunn returns to write and direct.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Reveals Best Look Yet at X-Men's Beast, And It's Actually Perfect
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel When the initial cast announcement video for Avengers: Doomsday was streamed, the names that stood out the most to everyone were the actors from the Fox era of X-Men films. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google When the initial cast announcement video for Avengers: Doomsday was streamed, the names that stood out the most to everyone were the actors from the Fox era of X-Men films. We were all expecting the likes of Chris Hemsworth, Florence Pugh, and Anthony Mackie, but Patrick Stewart, Ian McKellen, James Marsden, Rebecca Romijn, and Kelsey Grammer were complete surprises. Kelsey Grammer was especially surprising because his career has mostly seen him in smaller movies lately, yet he's back as Beast, aka Hank McCoy , in this blockbuster and we've just seen the best look at him in Avengers: Doomsday .

Over the past few months, trailers have been dropping for the movie, and we have seen a look at Cyclops, Professor X, Mystique, Magneto, and even Gambit. However, Beast had yet to appear until the most recent and final trailer. Even then, it was a quick look at him as he joined various other heroes after Cyclops said his iconic line, "To me, my X-Men ." Although it was only a glimpse, it was clear that Beast looked good. Now that we have a new, high quality image of the character, we can see that his appearance is much better than good. It's the perfect look for Beast.

Now that the final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday has arrived and the film is mere weeks away, promotion is ramping up. That includes a new special look put out by Entertainment Weekly , which also has several quotes from the stellar cast. One of the photos released is the shot of a close-up of Beast and he looks spectacular. The fur on his body looks pretty realistic, as does the hair around his face. His face is an excellent blend of looking like the sophisticated Kelsey Grammer and the more vicious side of the mutant.

That's difficult to pull off, but it works along the same lines as what the MCU has done with Mark Ruffalo and the Hulk. That has always looked good, so it makes sense that it feels the same for Beast. This looks like a Beast who can both verbally spar with geniuses like Shuri and Reed Richards, as well as one who can go toe-to-toe with whatever Doctor Doom throws at him. Grammer's first appearance in the MCU came as a surprise during the post-credit scene of The Marvels .

His look as Beast there was solid, though something was a bit off. It felt more like what we got back in the 2000s when the technology wasn't as advanced, yet now that has been fixed. Even so, his appearance in The Marvels was well received, which Grammer addressed with Entertainment Weekly , saying he heard "a lot of great response from that little cameo," which prompted Disney to bring him back for a larger role. Now that the character looks better than ever, people are even more excited about his return.

Beast is a character who hasn't been on the big screen since the X-Men prequels of the 2010s. His previous appearance came in Dark Phoenix , which was a poorly received film. While Nicholas Hoult was great in the role and his Beast looked impressive, this photo from Avengers: Doomsday suggests that we are about to see the perfect iteration of Beast to date.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Released by Steelers After 'Pat McAfee Show' Appearance
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers cut the four-time NFL Most Valuable Player on Wednesday, after comments he made about Steelers coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on the ESPN’s show.
articles.content:
Aaron Rodgers came to Pittsburgh in a Chevy.

He left it sitting atop a flamethrower.

The Pittsburgh Steelers cut the four-time NFL Most Valuable Player on Wednesday, shortly after he torched Steelers coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on ESPN’s The Pat McAfee Show .

The move capped a chaotic 18 hours in which the team announced it was benching the 42-year-old future Hall of Famer for backup Mason Rudolph ahead of Friday’s visit from Denver. Related Stories Business Tony Romo Lands Post-CBS Gig With Betting App Betr as "Chief Predictions Officer" (Exclusive) TV Tom Jackson, Denver Broncos' All-Pro Linebacker and ESPN Analyst, Dies at 75

Rodgers responded by taking an excused absence from the club, then used the unexpected time off to go on McAfee and repeatedly call the 62-year-old McCarthy’s mental state into question. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Rodgers told McAfee he found out about the surprise decision while on the phone with teammates, including tight end Pat Freiermuth.

It was just the start of a blistering offensive from Rodgers, who painted McCarthy — whom he played under during a long successful run in Green Bay earlier in their careers — as a leader woefully out of touch.

He described a quarterback meeting last Wednesday with McCarthy arriving late, sat down “and within 10 minutes began snoring,” woke up and nodded off again minutes later, then eventually “walks out of the room like nothing happened.” Rodgers also said McCarthy missed an offensive meeting Thursday, missed a walkthrough Friday and a morning meeting Saturday while not holding a team meeting that night.

“And then comes to Sunday, when obviously we struggled and the product wasn’t great,” Rodgers said, adding that McCarthy broke up the halftime locker room meeting by saying “1-2-3 Packers.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Rodgers said he felt it was the right thing to bring up the issues to McCarthy as a longtime league star instead of putting it on others with fewer years, shaky roster positions or those who “haven’t made $400 million dollars in the NFL.”

“Me? I don’t care, what are you going to do to me?” Rodgers said. “Like I said, you’re going to release me? Cool. You’re going to deflect this thing and make it that you were trying to bench me and that I’m at home contemplating whether or not I’m going to accept a benching? Couldn’t be farther from the truth.

“That word never came up in our meetings. What came up was: sleeping, habits, gameplan, understanding what we’re doing, being able to call a play, being able to call a game without the game sheet.”

The scene played out bizarrely during Rodgers’ extended appearance on the show in which he has been an occasional contributor. McCarthy waded through a throng of assembled reporters in the lobby — most of them huddled over their phones listening to Rodgers — after practice ended.

Minutes later in a subdued locker room, the Steelers left to pick up the pieces declined to get into specifics about Rodgers’ accusations but didn’t dismiss them either.

Asked if he’s confident McCarthy can lead the team going forward, Freiermuth responded with a simple “I’m confident” but little else.

Wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling, who played alongside Rodgers and under McCarthy as a rookie in Green Bay in 2018, acknowledged there was general frustration about the team’s recent performance but allowed “I didn’t think it was this.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Rodgers has already said this will be his last season. Now it’s fair to wonder if he’ll reach the end of it — in Pittsburgh anyway — after McCarthy turned to Rudolph, a longtime backup, with the Steelers (6-4) trying to snap out of a two-game funk before it’s too late.

There’s little precedent for sitting a future Hall of Famer and Super Bowl winner midseason. Johnny Unitas, playing out his final days in a Chargers uniform, got benched for rookie Dan Fouts after four games in 1973.

Joe Namath never played again after throwing four picks in a loss to Chicago during a late-career cameo for the Los Angeles Rams a month into the 1977 season.

More recently, Denver replaced Peyton Manning with Brock Osweiler midway through 2015 even with the club sitting at 7-2. Manning returned in the season finale and then served as a game manager in the playoffs as the Broncos’ dominant defense led the franchise to its third Super Bowl victory.

Manning walked off the field with the Lombardi Trophy in tow in his final game.

While the Steelers are currently in playoff position, their next three games are against AFC West-leading Denver, surging Houston, and AFC South leader Jacksonville. While they can probably withstand one loss or maybe even two, three could be catastrophic.

Enter Rudolph, who rescued Pittsburgh’s season and briefly earned folk hero status in 2023 by coming off the bench in December and authoring a surge to a playoff berth. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

That didn’t stop the Steelers from moving on from him immediately, bringing in Russell Wilson and Justin Fields in 2024 and then Rodgers in 2025, a move designed to help Pittsburgh end a postseason victory drought that’s nearing a decade.

Rodgers’ first year ended with a blowout playoff loss at home to the Texans. His future seemed uncertain until the Steelers hired McCarthy to replace Mike Tomlin in January, a job Rodgers played a hand in helping McCarthy land, though how big a hand is up for debate.

Not that it mattered in the end. Rodgers opted to make one last run at a championship while reuniting with the coach he won a Super Bowl with in early 2011.

A storybook ending on the field seems remote. Pittsburgh is a woeful 2-4 on the road, where it figures to be when the playoffs start if the Steelers can’t track down Cincinnati in the race for the AFC North title.

And the team’s Jekyll/Hyde play in general has offered little tangible proof that it is a legitimate threat to have an extended postseason stay.

Rodgers’ play has mirrored that of his team. He tossed three touchdowns in three consecutive weeks, even outdueling Cincinnati star Joe Burrow in a victory over the Bengals in late September.

Yet he’s struggled to make an impact of late, often checking the ball down to running backs Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle or taking sacks behind an inconsistent offensive line when trying to push the ball down the field to a receiving group that has underperformed, particularly two-time Pro Bowler DK Metcalf. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Rodgers averaged just 0.5 air yards per attempt in the first half last week against Philadelphia, the lowest since ESPN began measuring the stat in 2006.

What happens next to a player who has always leaned into doing things on his terms at all times is unclear. Pittsburgh was supposed to be his third and final NFL stop.

He seemed content on Tuesday, spending time in the locker room trading jokes with Rudolph and longtime defensive tackle Cam Heyward after addressing reporters.

Barely eight hours later, Rodgers was no longer the starter. Shortly after that, he was no longer a Steeler, the latest and perhaps final twist in a journey that will end with him getting a gold jacket at the Pro Football Hall of Fame, even if this ends up being an inglorious off-ramp for all involved.

articles.title: I’m So Glad Netflix’s The Body EPs Are Debunking Two Theories While We Await Word On Season 2

I'm so glad the EPs have also confirmed the Lions won't be going to jail after what happened to Grace. I thought that was a possibility, given Anya's confession and the various details about the party that came out toward the end of Season 1.

While I'm all for accountability in teen dramas, especially when it comes to Riverdale' s Archie Andrews , I'll let it slide for The Body . Sending Anya or any of the Lions to jail or prison for their actions at the party would've created a major genre shift in the story, and I'm far more interested in the story remaining around the school after Season 1's ending.

articles.summary: A game that launched on the original PlayStation console all the way back in 1996 has received an unexpected new release this week around the globe. While essentially all modern games now get worldwide releases across various platforms, this wasn't always the case. During the era of the PS1, specifically, a number of games ended […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A game that launched on the original PlayStation console all the way back in 1996 has received an unexpected new release this week around the globe. While essentially all modern games now get worldwide releases across various platforms, this wasn't always the case. During the era of the PS1, specifically, a number of games ended up launching only in Japan and never made their way to the United States, Europe, or other territories. Now, one PS1 game that has remained exclusive to Japan for three decades will be exclusive no longer thanks to the arrival of a new port.

Set to launch on November 26th, Mezase! Senkyu-Oh will be arriving across PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 platforms. Originally released in 1995, Mezase! Senkyu-Oh was initially an arcade puzzle title known as Battle Balls that was created by Seibu Kaihatsu. Battle Balls ended up being popular enough in Japanese arcades that it was eventually brought to North America in 1996. As such, this game is one that some in the United States might be familiar with.

However, it's the game's eventual PS1 port that never made its way outside of Japan. To capitalize on the success of Battle Balls , Seibu Kaihatsu re-released the game on PS1 in April of 1996 under the name Mezase! Senkyu-Oh . Although this home console version of Battle Balls was similar to the arcade iteration, the game never took off in the same way. As a result, Mezase! Senkyu-Oh remained exclusive to PS1 platforms in Japan in perpetuity.

" Mezase! Senkyu-Oh was released by Seibu Kaihatsu in 1996 for a 32-bit home console," says the game's new description. "This is a puzzle game where you connect 4 or more of the same type of Colored Ball falling from the top of the screen to clear them. Easy to control, anyone can experience the thrill of massive chain reactions!"

This new version of Mezase! Senkyu-Oh happens to be the latest release in Hamster's Console Archives program , which looks to bring back games from old-school consoles to modern hardware. Mezase! Senkyu-Oh is the latest such release in this initiative that happens to have revived a Japan-exclusive PS1 game and has brought it to other markets for the first time. When it launches on PS5 and Switch 2 within the coming day, Mezase! Senkyu-Oh will retail for $11.99 across both the PlayStation Store and Nintendo eShop.

How do you feel about the release of this throwback PS1 game on new platforms for the first time? And will you be picking up Mezase! Senkyu-Oh for yourself, or will instead be skipping out on this new Console Archives release? Be sure to let me know down in the comments section.

articles.title: Andy Taylor, Duran Duran Guitarist, Dies at 65
articles.summary: He served as the band's guitarist during their commercial height and later became a founding member of the supergroup The Power Station.
articles.content:
Andy Taylor, Duran Duran 's guitarist during the band's commercial peak in the 1980s as well as a founding member of supergroup the Power Station, has died. He was 65

Taylor died following a battle with prostate cancer, his family and Duran Duran announced on social media Wednesday.

"To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather," his wife Tracey Taylor said in a statement. "He was the rock of our family. For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first. Nothing made him happier than having us all together, and no matter how far music took him, his heart was always at home." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Lifestyle Veruschka, Mesmerizing Supermodel of the 1960s and '70s, Dies at 87 TV Steven Hack, Original 'Cats' Castmember and Busy Onscreen Character Actor, Dies at 68

As the band said in a statement of its own: "Andy was there at the very beginning of our story. From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed."

Taylor wasn't technically a founding member of Duran Duran, but he joined the group in 1980 before they recorded their eponymous 1981 debut album, and he served as the guitarist through the band's commercial zenith on sophomore album Rio and third album Seven and the Ragged Tiger before he left amidst the recording of the group's fourth album Notorious. He re-joined Duran Duran from 2001 to 2006, and he appeared on the band's 2023 album Danse Macabre as well. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Taylor co-wrote several of the band's biggest hits including " Hungry Like the Wolf," "Rio" and "Girls on Film." He was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame with the group in 2022. His battle with cancer had prevented Taylor from attending the induction ceremony, with the group reading a letter Taylor wrote instead.

"I’m proud of everything we’ve achieved together and of the way you have continued," he said at the time. "As a guitar player in a progressive band from the synth days of the early eighties, literally from the day I met Nick, John, Simon and Roger they truly valued the contribution of a rather noisy, versatile Northern brat."

"I'm so very proud of these four brothers," he continued. "I'm amazed at their durability, and I'm overjoyed at accepting this award. I often doubted the day would come. I'm sure as hell glad I'm around to see the day."

The news comes weeks after the band confirmed drummer Roger Taylor would leave the group due to ongoing struggles with tinnitus. In an extensive statement, frontman Simon Le Bon lauded Taylor for his versatility, noting that he "can play it like Mick Ronson, or he can play it like Jimmy Paige, he can even play rinky-dink rhythm like Nile Rodgers. But what he does most is play guitar like guitar-genius — Andy Taylor!"

"Me & him had a special bond right from the start," Le Bon said. "He's the one who gave me my band name — 'Charley.' And after 2006, when he wasn't touring with us, we spent happy days at the studio in his Ibiza villa, laying down tracks for our latest records. I have so many wonderful, hilarious, tragic memories of our time together: on tour, in the studio, in our little flat on Caroline Road, Balsall Heath at 6am. And through it, & above it all he was in love with his family — most important thing in his life. There's a massive Andy Taylor shaped hole in my heart. It'll never close up; I won't let it. I will miss him & love him for all my days.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Fellow Duran Duran and Power Station member John Taylor called Andy Taylor "a demon, a killer riff-merchant, melodist, six string textualist (he would hate that term) and a singer with a great voice."

"What he brought down to Birmingham on that train from Whitley Bay can never be quantified," he said. "Spirit! What a lark we had, and great records."

Nick Rhodes paid tribute with a poem that concluded with "Goodbye demon fire, live wire."

Roger Taylor said that "the sadness cuts extremely deep, but admiration and respect run even deeper for the Taylor that wasn't related but will forever be my brother. Rest in peace now, Andy."

The band said Taylor's family has requested that in lieu of flowers, donations be made in Taylor's name to Prostate Cancer U.K.

Along with his wife Tracey, Taylor is survived by his children Georgina, Isabella, Bethany and Andrew, and grandson Albie. "Andy faced the last few years with so much courage and determination," Tracey Taylor said in a statement. "He never gave up, fighting until the very end, never losing his love of life. The kindness and support shown to him by fans from all over the world throughout his illness brought him immense comfort and strength, and for that we will always be grateful."

articles.title: Rockstar Finally Explains One of Its Most Divisive Decisions With GTA 6
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Rockstar Games Even with a suite of new features, Grand Theft Auto 6 still has plenty of the series' DNA coursing through its Vice City veins, as seen in its Wanted system, weapon wheel, and crime-filled narrative. However, it's missing one feature players have come to expect: the ability to replay missions. Rockstar Games has a reason […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Even with a suite of new features, Grand Theft Auto 6 still has plenty of the series' DNA coursing through its Vice City veins, as seen in its Wanted system, weapon wheel , and crime-filled narrative. However, it's missing one feature players have come to expect: the ability to replay missions. Rockstar Games has a reason for its exclusion, though.

Speaking to Kotaku , senior design director Scott Butchard said the team had mulled over the idea but ultimately decided against it. In his view, being able to warp around time would downplay some of the game's story.

“Mission replay was certainly something we looked at early on in development, and we do not currently support it,” said Butchard. “As the game came together it felt at odds with the story we were trying to tell and felt a bit alien and disconnected. Sitting outside of the game as it were and replaying missions really diminished the choices you had made.”

It's an interesting response, especially since this has been in Rockstar's games since the Ballad of Gay Tony expansion for Grand Theft Auto 4 in 2009. Since then, Red Dead Redemption , L.A. Noire , Max Payne 3 , Grand Theft Auto 5 , and Red Dead Redemption 2 have all supported the ability to go back and play old missions again, often with the goal of ticking off optional objectives. The latter two titles in particular were seemingly built around being replayed, as their 100% completion percentages were tediously locked behind achieving the numerous amount of gold medals.

Since all of these titles let players warp around, it would seem as though Butchard's words could be applied to any of those games, too. For example, does being able to replay missions in Red Dead Redemption 2 not trivialize the more gut-wrenching sacrifices in the latter half? Regardless, it seems as though this disconnect makes for a decent reason to not add the ability to replay missions in GTA 6 , which would create a lot of extra work for the studio. It is already a massive game , too.

It doesn't seem likely mission replay will be added in the future through an update. Anything is possible, but Butchard never hinted it was coming, after all. However, it's plausible someone will mod it into the PC port in the future, which seems to be coming sooner rather than later . Even if the unofficial mod comes to PC version, console players will probably have to resort to keeping separate manual saves in order to relive some of GTA 6 's most bombastic or memorable moments.

Would you like the ability to replay missions in GTA 6 ? Or are you just waiting for the online multiplayer? Share your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: Why Is Netflix’s Guarding Stars A Christmas Movie When Its Book Is Not? I Asked Jared Padalecki
articles.summary: I had to ask the star of The Bodyguard's adaptation.
articles.content:
Katherine Center’s novel, The Bodyguard, is not about Christmas. Not even a little bit. So, when I learned its book-to-screen adaptation , Guarding Stars , was part of Netflix’s 2026 Christmas movie lineup , I was confused. So, I had to ask Jared Padalecki why they decided to involve the holiday in this film.

Listen, while there are some great Thanksgiving movies, Christmas movies are talked about way more, and there’s a ton of buzz around them. Folks love the most wonderful time of the year, and Netflix figured more people would tune into Guarding Stars if it was centered around Christmas instead of another holiday.

I think they accomplished this goal too. While Guarding Stars is quite different from its source material (the change at the end surprised me), Jack and Hannah, at their cores, are the same. The spirit of the book is 100% in the movie, and it feels very true to the source material in that way.

So, that’s why Guarding Stars is a Christmas movie even though The Bodyguard has nothing to do with it. Moving it back to take place in December puts it in a category of films that people flock to at this time of year as they prepare for the holidays. No other holiday can do that at such a high level. So, this change does make a lot of sense.

articles.title: 6 Of The Comfiest Comfort Movies Of All Time Are Streaming In The Same Place
articles.summary: Grab a blanket and some hot chocolate!
articles.content:
I don't need the weather to be cold in order to feel the urge to cuddle up under a blanket and watch my favorite feel-good comfort movies... but it helps. With the hustle and bustle of the holiday season upon us, I'm keeping a close eye out for films that transport me right to my happy place, and it just so happens that there are several top-tier comfort movies that are all streaming in the same place.

Ok, grab a blanket and settle in, because these comfort movies are all streaming on Peacock:

I'm going to sandwich this list with holiday movies, because 'tis the season, and love actually is all around. Richard Curtis's beloved and star-studded Christmas rom-com tells the story of several characters facing a variety of struggles with love. Between the romance, the humor and the magical UK backdrop during the holiday season, Love, Actually is non-stop good, cozy vibes from start to finish.

If rom-coms set in London (or Hugh Grant movies) are your thing, you can pair Love, Actually with a screening of Notting Hill . The extremely quotable 1999 rom-com stars Grant as a bookshop owner who meets and falls for a famous American actress (played by Julia Roberts). Its charming romance and delightful cast make Notting Hill the perfect movie to curl up and watch any time of the year.

As timeless classics go, The Princess Bride is among the elite. Blending fantasy with comedy and romance, the 1987 movie stars Cary Elwes and Robin Wright as the central characters of a story being read by a grandfather to his grandson. Not only is The Princess Bride one to watch (or rewatch over and over ) with the whole family, it's an easy go-to comfort movie when you just feel like feeling all of the feelings.

I've mentioned a lot of rom-coms on this list, as the genre and comfy go hand in snuggly hand. Still, let's shift gears for a bit of romance in the form of a period drama. A good adaptation of a Jane Austen book might just be the gold standard there, and this one is particularly rewatchable . Peacock has Joe Wright's 2005 adaptation of Pride and Prejudice streaming. This is the version of the love story that stars Keira Knightley and Matthew Macfadyen as Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy, respectively.

Who doesn't adore a great second-chance romance story? Reese Witherspoon shines in this 2002 rom-com about a designer who returns to her southern hometown to finalize her divorce. While she and her ex (played by Josh Lucas ) instantly butt heads, they also discover the spark that once seemed lost. If funny and romantic with a bit of Southern charm is what you're after, stream Sweet Home Alabama on Peacock right now.

I told you I was sandwiching this list with holiday movies, and here we are with a Christmas classic . I'm closing this out with one of my own personal favorites: Frank Capra's It's a Wonderful Life . I will never tire of revisiting this movie at least once a year to see George Bailey (James Stewart) discover the value of the life he's lived. While the overall message of the movie is inspirational, the way it's told -- George's guardian angel is tasked with saving him, but before he can do that, he's learning about George's life by visiting several pivotal moments -- that makes this movie such a great comfort watch.

But the 44-year-old, who also produces the movie, found the role to be more difficult than he'd expected.

"Jack Stapleton in this world is super famous," he tells The Hollywood Reporter about this character. "He's Brad Pitt, he's George Clooney, he's Chris Hemsworth — people who can't walk outside. He admits that he'll often encounter people in public who stop him to share their love for Supernatural or Gilmore Girls , but he's still able to go to his son's games or his daughter's field hockey practices. It helps, certainly, that he and his wife, actress and fellow Guarding Stars producer Genevieve Padalecki, live in a ranch outside Austin, Texas, rather than in Los Angeles.

Guarding Stars , released on the streamer on Nov. 18, is based on Katherine Center's romance novel The Bodyguard and features a delightful role reversal. Rather than Padalecki, who's spent much of his adult life starring in action-driven projects, as the dutiful protector, his character Jack finds himself under the care of bodyguard Hannah Brooks, played by Leighton Meester.

The book, while not set at Christmas, has the same spirit as its onscreen adaptation. articles.title: 5 Terrible Pokemon Winds and Waves Can Save With an Evolution
articles.summary: With over 1,000 Pokemon, it is inevitable that some are going to be considerably worse than others. Even with the idea that every Pokemon may be someone's favorite, it is difficult to justify using some in a mainline playthrough, let alone in competitive Pokemon. Poor stats, disappointing move pools, underwhelming abilities, and unfortunate type combinations […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google With over 1,000 Pokemon, it is inevitable that some are going to be considerably worse than others. Even with the idea that every Pokemon may be someone's favorite, it is difficult to justify using some in a mainline playthrough, let alone in competitive Pokemon. Poor stats, disappointing move pools, underwhelming abilities, and unfortunate type combinations can leave otherwise interesting Pokemon collecting dust in a PC box. But Game Freak has repeatedly shown it can make bad Pokemon good with a second chance, and this is exactly what Pokemon Winds and Waves can do.

Some of the most exciting additions to new Pokemon generations are evolutions for existing Pokemon. Annihilape, Kingambit, and Farigiraf all great examples of how Game Freak can breathe new life into familiar Pokemon and improve their usage. These evolutions helped take awful or forgotten Pokemom and brought them into the spotlight. Not every Pokemon needs to become a competitive powerhouse, but there should at least be a compelling reason to include one on your team. With that in mind, these are five of the worst Pokemon that deserve redemption with an evolution Pokemon Winds and Waves .

Sunflora is truly one of the most forgettable and useless Pokemon. This Generation 2 Grass-type Pokemon has a base stat total of 425, with only its 105 special attack being good. It gets a few coverage options and supportive moves, but that is about the only positives. It is far too slow for Chlorophyll to be useful, and Solar Power isn't much better as far as abilities go. If you are using a Grass-type Pokemon in sun, there are far better options.

A Grass and Fire-type evolution seems like the perfect direction for Sunflora, especially if Game Freak gives it a different niche than Scovillain. Giving it more Fire-type attacks, better speed and special attack would make it a decent user for Chlorophyll, or Game Freak could opt for a new ability altogether. Likewise, with these changes, Solar Power becomes a more viable option. These changes could make it more offensive than Scovillain and its more defensive Mega Evolution.

Another option would be to keep Sunflora's low speed and make it a strong Trick Room attacker. Game Freak could still make it Grass and Fire-type and perhaps give it a signature Grass-type spread move similar to Eruption or Heatwave. This would certainly go a long way toward making it unique and would give more recognition and respect to a Pokemon that has been sidelined since Pokemon Gold and Silver .

Carnivine easily has one of the best and most wasted designs in Pokemon, but there is little reason to use it over any other Grass-type Pokemon. It was introduced in Pokemon Diamond and Pearl , and while it has decent offensive stats, the rest of its stats are just bad. Then there is its ability, Levitate, which makes it immune to a type it already resists. Carnivine is one of the best examples of wasted potential in the series, and it desperately needs a buff in Winds and Waves .

The best way to improve Carnivine through an evolution would be to give it a new ability, one that functions like Shadow Tag that prevents Ghost-type Pokemon from switching out at the cost of allowing Grass-type Pokemon to switch out. This would bring a new dynamic to Perish Trap teams and give Carnivine one of the most unique abilities. With a stat boost and better coverage moves, this could give Carnivine a great niche.

Alternatively, Game Freak could lean into a Grass and Poison-type Pokemon if it wants to justify Levitate. It would need a significant boost to its stats if this is the route taken and it could even function like Toxipex. This role would make it annoying and bulky Pokemon that poisons opponents and uses attacking moves, perhaps a Grass-type version of Infestation, to trap Pokemon on the field. It has a fantastic design and an evolution could further improve this as well as make it more useable.

Castform might be one of the biggest examples of a fantastic Pokemon concept wasted by poor stats. Introduced in Pokemon Ruby and Sapphire , Castform changes its appearance and typing in response to certain weather conditions through its Forecast ability. But this really cool feature is ruined by Castform's terrible stats which total out to 420. Considering how important weather has become in competitive Pokemon battles, it is disappointing that the Pokemon specifically designed around weather manipulation is so thoroughly outclassed in any weather type.

An evolution with increased speed and special attack would turn Castform into a strong Weather Ball user. It already has great coverage, so giving it more supportive moves would also be a great choice. Game Freak could even give it a new signature move that changes effect based on the weather that is different from Weather Ball, perhaps having a heightened chance at status conditions. Castform also needs a Rock-type form when sand is active, which definitely feels like an oversight.

Another option is to alter the Forecast ability altogether, adjusting the stats based on the active weather. Alternatively, the ability could be buffed to increase a stat when weather is changed, allowing Castform to function in weather you set and weather set by the opponent. This would bring a new dynamic to weather wars, as you risk powering up Castform throughout the battle. With such a unique gimmick, and Winds and Waves rumored focus on weather , Castform desperately needs some love from Game Freak.

Spinda is one of the most unique Pokemon, as Game Freak has given it billions of possible spot patterns. But it is so terrible that players have almost never even bothered to use it, let alone collect different spot variants. Introduced in Pokemon Ruby and Sapphire , Spinda has a base stat total of 360, with 60 points distributed into each stat. Not only does this leave the Normal-type with no strengths, it can only be considered a weakness in every single category.

Spinda has a great ability already in Contrary, and so an evolution could keep this. The main thing this Pokemon needs is increased stats and a simple 20 points put into each stat, to keep the theme going, would do a lot for it. This would put it on par with Malamar and when combined with Contrary, it could become a decently dangerous Pokemon. It already has great moves in Fake Out, Encore, Disable, and plenty of other supportive moves along side a decent choice of coverage options.

An extra 20 points into its stats wouldn't make it broken by any means. Game Freak could even give it an additional typing, like Fighting, to give it more versatility. This would also allow it to use Superpower or Close Combat and become a strong Contrary user, especially if paired with Baton Pass. Spinda is without a gimmick Pokemon, but this doesn't mean it can't be useful. Winds and Waves could give Spinda a more interesting evolution without having it take over the meta.

Wobbuffet is one of the strangest Pokemon Game Freak has ever designed. Introduced in Pokemon Gold and Silver , this Psychic-type Pokemon has an impressive base HP stat of 190, but its remaining stats are dreadful. But that isn't even the worst part. Its entire strategy revolves around anticipating an opponent's attacks and retaliating with Counter or Mirror Coat. The only saving grace for Wobbuffet is its ability, Shadow Tag, but there are plenty of better Pokemon that get access to this ability.

Rather than abandoning Wobbuffet's unusual gimmick, Game Freak should embrace it with an evolution. Increasing its Defense and Special Defense while giving it more supportive moves, such as Follow Me, Taunt, Disable, Helping Hand, Trick Room, and more could make it an excellent partner when paired with Shadow Tag. This would still make its only damaging function be countering, but it would give Wobbuffet something to do while sitting on the field in competitive play. In single-player playthroughs, it would probably need at least one damaging move though.

Wobbuffet is one of the most recognizable Pokemon thanks to its role in the Pokemon anime . It did get a pre-evolution in Wynaut, but this is only a worse version of an already awful Pokemon. Giving it an evolution in Winds and Waves would go a long way toward putting in the spotlight. Wobbuffet is a unique concept of a Pokemon and it would be a shame to see continue to sit in the trash when fixing it is an easy task. Making it more bulky and supportive is the best option for turning this Psychic Pokemon into a good one.

articles.title: ‘Hoppers’ Director Daniel Chong Talks Blending Chaos With Heart; Teases Pixar’s ‘Ghost Market’

articles.content:
Daniel Chong cannot stop working with animals. His storyboarding credits span Toy Story shorts, Cars 2 , Dr. Seuss’s The Lorax and Inside Out , to name a few, but his first creator credit came with Cartoon Network’s Emmy-nominated We Bare Bears . As an Asian American creative in the industry, Chong explored social anxieties, friendship, assimilation, self-care and belonging through three bear brothers’ attempts to fit into human society. Now back at Pixar as a director, he brings those sensibilities to his first theatrical feature, Hoppers , and punches them up several notches.

With environmentalism at its center, the film follows animal lover Mabel Tanaka ( Piper Curda ) as she tries to rehabilitate a local glade that was special to her and her late grandmother. To succeed, Mabel transfers her consciousness into an animatronic beaver and goes undercover in the animal world. Then all beaver dams break loose. The deeper Mabel goes, the more she uncovers the dynamics of the natural world, including those shaped by the pond’s ruler, Prince George ( Bobby Moynihan ), which causes her simple plan to save the glade to go awry. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Casting Dave Franco & Willa Fitzgerald To Lead Lionsgate Horror Film 'Mommy's Home' News Meryl Streep, Jon Hamm, Dave Franco Brought Comedy To 'Hoppers', Director Daniel Chong Says - Contenders L.A.

It’s a fun and heartfelt adventure that arguably breaks the mold of Pixar’s more conventional releases. The film features a great white shark assassin ( Vanessa Bayer ), wildlife happily coming to terms with their own deaths, and a caterpillar (Eman Abdul-Razzak/ Dave Franco ) hellbent on revenge and domination. Chong and writer Jesse Andrews give the comedy room to run wild while making space for the beauty and importance of the natural world—and for the struggle to protect what you care about, open yourself up to others and find a community that supports you.
